harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a btrfs-backed, fstab-persisted loopback filesystem at /srv/data on node1 (Alpine Linux, single ext4 root disk with no native snapshot support). Populated it with application data, took a read-only btrfs snapshot, modified/corrupted the live data, then restored /srv/data to the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot via subvolume swap, verified byte-identical via sha256 checksums. Completed the mandatory single-node restart cycle: captured pre-reboot boot identity and health, rebooted node1, confirmed a new boot_id post-reboot, and verified the fstab-mounted /srv/data plus both btrfs subvolumes (live data and the baseline snapshot) survived and remained healthy.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine Linux 3.23, single ext4 root disk, no LVM/btrfs/zfs tooling present
Installed btrfs-progs via apk
Created a 4G loopback image /var/lib/srv-data-backing/srv-data.img, formatted as btrfs, created a 'data' subvolume
Mounted /srv/data via /etc/fstab using loop,subvol=data options for persistence across reboots
Populated /srv/data/app with config.yaml, accounts.csv, audit.log and recorded sha256 checksums as the baseline
Created a read-only btrfs snapshot (subvolume ID 257) of the data subvolume capturing the baseline state
Modified /srv/data: deleted accounts.csv, overwrote config.yaml, appended to audit.log, added a rogue malware.txt file
Restored /srv/data by unmounting, deleting the mutated subvolume, and creating a fresh writable snapshot from the read-only baseline snapshot
Verified restored checksums matched the original baseline exactly and the rogue file was gone
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed healthy mount/data state as baseline
Rebooted node1 via 'reboot', with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned and confirmed boot_id changed, proving a genuine restart
Verified post-restart: /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab, file checksums still match the restored baseline, and both btrfs subvolumes (live data and snapshot) persisted

evidence.summary: Confirmed no native snapshot tooling existed, installed btrfs-progs, built and formatted a loopback btrfs image, and mounted it as /srv/data with a 'data' subvolume.
Added an /etc/fstab entry using loop,subvol=data and verified a clean umount/mount -a round trip mounts /srv/data correctly.

evidence.requirement: Baseline application data and snapshot captured
evidence.summary: Wrote config.yaml, accounts.csv, audit.log to /srv/data/app, recorded sha256 checksums, then created read-only btrfs snapshot ID 257 of the data subvolume.
Deleted accounts.csv, overwrote config.yaml, appended to audit.log, and added malware.txt; checksums confirm divergence from baseline.

evidence.requirement: Exact restoration of earlier snapshot content
evidence.summary: Deleted mutated subvolume, created new writable snapshot from the read-only baseline snapshot; sha256 checksums of restored files exactly match the original baseline (cmd-47ae31547d9f4d41), malware.txt is gone, config.yaml/accounts.csv content restored.
Captured boot_id 34abf93f-a408-4f81-a5f9-7bb344ff8724, confirmed /srv/data mounted with restored, checksum-matching data, and fstab entry present.
Issued backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' so the acknowledgement returned before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving genuine restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Connection failures during the outage window followed by successful reconnection showing boot_id c2e9243c-f805-4b8a-bc96-efe68bf8ea9e, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, and a fresh uptime since 2026-09-29 09:50:04.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of data and snapshot state (node1)
evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/data auto-mounted via fstab after reboot with checksums still matching the restored baseline, and both btrfs subvolumes (live data ID 258, read-only snapshot ID 257) intact.
